adminGuide.title: Site operations guide
adminGuide.intro: Common settings and workflows that guild operators often miss. Each section links directly to where you can edit it.

eventLifecycle.title: Event lifecycle
eventLifecycle.step1: Create event: fill in time/location/notes. Saved as draft initially.
eventLifecycle.step2: Configure parties/slots: load a template or add parties → set role, gear, and spec per slot.
eventLifecycle.step3: Publish: use the banner button to move the event to a state where members can apply.
eventLifecycle.step4: Mark battle started: press the 'Battle Started' button to lock battle_started_at. Regear window timer begins from this moment.
eventLifecycle.step5: After the event: the auto-regear cron reads killboard and generates approvals. Members can submit manual regear once the window opens.

regear.title: Regear system
regear.body: Auto (killboard-based) and manual (screenshot-based) regear coexist. Per-role cap (role_rewards.silver) of 0 blocks all regear for that role.
regear.bullet1: The auto-regear toggle is a global switch. It must be ON for the cron to convert killboard deaths into approvals.
regear.bullet2: Slot editor has 'Exclude from auto-regear' (visible only when global ON) and 'Exclude from manual regear' (always) checkboxes for per-build opt-out.
regear.bullet3: Regear window = N minutes after battle start. Max screenshot 10MB, PNG/JPEG/WebP only.
regear.bullet4: Auto-generated pending rows let the claimant edit per-slot prices. Admins review at /admin/dashboard/regear.

onboarding.title: Albion nickname verification
onboarding.body:
New members see an Albion server/nickname onboarding modal after login. On successful verification, both the site and Discord guild nicknames sync to the Albion name.

Verification requires an 'Albion home guild ID' set in Settings → Events tab. Without it, identities are stored but left unverified (verifiedAt=null).

The Stats page shows unverified/pending members. The 'Re-onboard' button clears a member's albion_* fields so the modal shows again.

bombSquad.title: Bomb-squad party & caller
bombSquad.body:
Bomb-squad parties use a 'members apply freely → caller approves/direct-assigns' flow. To use it:

1) Go to Settings → Permissions and configure at least one caller role.
2) Have at least one guild member with that role.
3) In the event party editor, toggle 'Bomb Squad' on and pick a caller.

Callers get a dedicated edit page at /events/{id}/party/{n} where they manage their own party's slots and members.

shop.title: Guild shop
shop.body:
Members exchange points for gear. Stock syncs via manual 'log paste' (ShopImportForm).

Silver↔point exchange rate (discount_rate) is a discount on a 1:1 base. 100% means silver price = point price; 50% sells for half.

AODP price warnings (quality/window/bluezone/redzone) surface when auto-regear suspects a problematic row.

notifications.title: Discord notifications
notifications.body:
Two delivery channels: event channel announcements and personal DMs.

- Event channel: configured via notify_channel_id + notify_role_id (role mention). Sent via a manual button on event create/edit.
- Personal DM: auto-sent 35 min before event to assigned members. Users can opt out in /me/settings.
- Regear/exchange approvals also DM the requester.

Requires DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN, DISCORD_EVENT_CHANNEL_ID, DISCORD_GUILD_ID env vars.

stats.title: Stats & monitoring
stats.body: Top/bottom point holders, event participation, shop/regear activity, and Albion verification status in one page. Use the inline 'Re-onboard' button to restart the onboarding flow for unverified members.

tips.title: Operation tips
tips.tip1: Before big changes, review global toggles (auto-regear, auto-start) in Settings.
tips.tip2: Save slot layouts as templates at /admin/dashboard/templates. Load quickly from the event editor.
tips.tip3: Use the party editor's 'Hide party' button to hide in-progress parties from the public page.
tips.tip4: For data issues, query Supabase Dashboard SQL editor directly. The 3 core tables: guild_avatars, regear_requests, point_ledger.

onboard.title: Install the bot on your Discord server
onboard.description: Pick a server where you have Manage Server permission to install the bot.
onboard.emptyDescription: You need the "Manage Server" permission on a Discord server to install the bot.
onboard.expiredDescription: Please log in again to refresh your Discord server list.
onboard.setupDescription: Configure member roles and the announcement channel for the newly installed guild.
onboard.memberRoleHelp: Only Discord users with this role can log in (multi-select allowed).
onboard.adminRoleHelp: Users with this role get all admin privileges (multi-select allowed).
onboard.channelHelp: Default Discord channel used when announcing new events (overridable per event).
onboard.unauthorized: You are not authorized to configure this guild.
onboard.missingRoles: Please select at least one member role.
onboard.albionStepDescription: Pick the server and "our guild" used for killboard verification and member onboarding. Guild UUIDs differ per server, so these two values are saved as a pair.
onboard.albionServerHelp: Select the shard your guild actually plays on. Changing server clears the selected guild.
onboard.albionHomeGuildHelp: Search by guild name and pick from the list. Leaving this empty saves all members as [unverified]; you can change it later in settings.
onboard.albionNoHomeGuild: Not set — all onboardings will be saved as [unverified].
onboard.rewardsStepDescription: Default regear payout cap per role. Used as the starting value for auto-regear approval and manual regear. Enter plain numbers (silver).
onboard.rewardsSilverHelp: Non-negative integer. You can change these anytime in admin settings.
onboard.rewardsErrorInvalidSilver: Silver must be a non-negative integer.
onboard.rewardsEmpty: Could not load role rewards. You can add them manually in settings after finishing.
onboard.completionBannerDescription: Basic setup is saved. You can fine-tune more knobs in the settings page.

battleTracking.settingsDescription: Polls public Albion battles every 15 minutes and records battles your home guild participated in. Opponents that haven't joined the app yet are still logged — once they join, past matches are backfilled retroactively.
battleTracking.enabledDescription: Turning this off stops collection immediately. Previously recorded battles are kept.
battleTracking.sizeDescription: A battle is only recorded when both sides fall in the same size bracket. Mixed brackets (e.g. small vs zerg) are skipped.
battleTracking.tipMatch: A side with fewer than 10 players is excluded. Battles are recorded only when both sides land in the same bracket (small/medium/large/zerg).
battleTracking.tipOutcome: Win/loss is decided by total kill fame per side. More fame = win, less = loss, equal = tie.
battleTracking.tipBackfill: Turning tracking on rescans stored battles and retroactively imports the ones your guild was part of.
battleTracking.tipLimitation: Sides are grouped by alliance. In messy multi-guild fights without alliances, the "opponent" aggregate may be over-counted.
battleTracking.listDescription: Public battles your guild participated in, newest first. Filter by size or outcome.
battleTracking.empty: No battle records yet. Enable tracking and select sizes — battles are added as the 15-minute cron runs and your guild enters fights.
